method: Only the cpu and cpuN lines of the paste are read; blank lines, comments and every other line such as intr, ctxt and btime are ignored. A line whose label already appeared in the current sample starts the second sample, so a paste of two consecutive cat /proc/stat captures is split without a separator, and a third sample is refused. Each line is read as four to ten whole-number counters in the documented order: user, nice, system, idle, iowait, irq, softirq, steal, guest and guest_nice; a missing tail column counts as zero. Because the counters are totals since boot, only the difference between the two samples is used. A counter that went backwards is clamped to zero, which the kernel allows for iowait, and the page reports how many counters were clamped. For each CPU total is the sum of the first eight differences, idle is idle plus iowait, and busy is total minus idle, so user, nice, system, irq, softirq and steal add up to busy and time waiting on I/O is reported under both iowait and idle rather than as busy. Guest and guest_nice are shown as shares of host time and are not added to total a second time. Every share is that difference divided by total, rounded half up to one decimal; an exact half therefore reads up, not to even. Idle is the exact complement of busy, so the two always add to 100. The all-CPU row is the aggregate cpu line when it is present and otherwise the sum of the per-CPU differences. The window is the all-CPU difference divided by 100 ticks per second and by the number of CPUs, which assumes USER_HZ of 100 (sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK)) and a CPU list that did not change between the reads; it is an estimate, and no window is shown when the paste has only the aggregate line. The page reads only the pasted text: it does not query the host, and it does not model steal, CPU frequency, thermal throttling or cgroup quota, so the shares are time shares as the kernel accounts them and not a diagnosis of the machine. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is sent, stored or uploaded.
